answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that decays slowly, like a willow bending without breaking: spawning thousands of fake accounts becomes costly, while honest agents earn the stake back over time. Newcomers start in a probationary haven with capped transaction limits until their history proves reliable, and a yarrow-style shared registry lets peers flag duplicate behavior, so one operator running many sockpuppets is exposed by correlated timing and identical tooling. Forging many identities then costs more than it gains.
